articles.title: A España se le sigue resistiendo el oro mundial en hockey
articles.standfirst: Jugó una gran final pero pagó cara su falta de acierto ante una Alemania que aprovechó un desafortunado rebote para revalidar la corona. Enorme campeonato de los de Max Caldas
articles.summary: Jugó una gran final pero pagó cara su falta de acierto ante una Alemania que aprovechó un desafortunado rebote para revalidar la corona. Enorme campeonato de los de Max Caldas
articles.body: "Cabeza y corazón" arengaba Marc Miralles, capitán de la selección española de hockey, en el círculo previo a la final del Mundial de hockey. Y los 'Redsticks' pusieron ambos en el Belfius Hockey Arena de Wavre (Bélgica), pero les faltó el gol. A la tercera no fue la vencida y a España se le volvió a escapar el oro mundial. La primera vez fue en Barcelona 1971 por un penalti córner, la segunda en Utrecht 1998 por un gol de oro en la prórroga y hoy, pese a que los de Max Caldas hicieron un gran partido ante Alemania, un gol de Michel Strurhoff en el tercer cuarto dejó a los 'Redsticks' a las puertas de la historia. La plata, que es la cuarta medalla mundial española para la selección masculina, devuelve a los ‘Redsticks’ al podio en una Copa del Mundo 20 años después de aquel bronce en 2006 en Mönchengladbach (Alemania), pero sobre todo deja muy buenas sensaciones a dos años de Los Ángeles 2028. Se marcha de Wavre con la cabeza muy alta y con la sensación de que mereció más. Porque España se plantó en la final habiendo dejado por el camino a favoritos como el campeón olímpico Países Bajos o Bélgica, líder del ranking mundial. Y aunque Caldas no quiere hablar de milagro, sólo comparar el número de licencias nos da una idea de la dimensión de la plata. En España hay 16.988 frente a las 220.000 fichas de los neerlandeses o a las 85.000 de los germanos, tetracampeones mundiales, plata olímpica en París 2024 y campeones de Europa. Este domingo, los 'Redsticks' saltaron al campo con la medalla asegurada en el bolsillo -faltaba por saber el color- para volver a disputar una final mundialista 28 años después. El equipo estaba convencido de que podían hacerlo porque España ya había batido a su rival en la segunda fase de este mismo campeonato. El primer cuarto de la final comenzó con dominio germano. La primera ocasión llegó con una penetración alemana que forzó el primer penalti-córner al minuto y medio. Tiro centrado de Benedikt Schwarzhaupt que sacó Luis Calzado evitando el primero. España empezó a combinar bien y en el minuto 9, Marc Reyné sacó petróleo desde la línea de fondo cuando se había quedado sin salida de la bola y provocó un penalti córner. Fue bien bloqueado por los alemanes, que montaron un contragolpe peligroso pero, por suerte, el disparo acabó fuera de los tres palos que defiende Calzado. Después de un primer cuarto de tanteo y sin goles, España comenzó el segundo mostrándose muy sólida en la presión y en la defensa de medio campo, pero le faltaba convertir las recuperaciones en ataques peligrosos. Sí lo logró en dos ocasiones que fueron desbaratadas por Danneberg. La primera a un gran tiro de Borja Lacalle y la segunda, de ‘Chefo’ Basterra, que se marcha del Mundial con siete goles, pero cuya acción fue anulada al darle por el lado curvo del stick. Alemania respondió al empuje español, pero los goles no llegaron por ninguno de los dos bandos y ambos equipos se fueron al descanso con empate a cero. Los 'RedSticks' se iban al vestuario dejando muy buenas sensaciones, sólo faltaba el gol. Cuatro ocasiones por su parte, dos por la alemana y con una posesión prácticamente al 50% para ambos. Todo por decidir. Tras el descanso, llegaron los mejores minutos de España, que dominaba el partido entrando por ambas bandas. La primera ocasión de gol llegó nada más empezar el tercer cuarto. La cruzó Cunill, la bola pasó entre dos jugadores alemanes y le llegó a Basterra, que no la esperaba y no acertó a rematar. Los de Max Caldas generaban más peligro, pero se les seguía resistiendo el gol. Una gran contra de Pol Cabré provocó el penalti-córner y el disparo de Marc Miralles casi se cantó como gol, pero la bola salió rozando el palo izquierdo. En los mejores momentos españoles llegó el gol de Alemania. Quedaba menos de un minuto y medio para acabar el tercer cuarto y Michel Struthoff recogió una bola suelta en el área pequeña, que había rebotado accidentalmente en el pie de Pepe Cunill, y solo ante Calzado le batió a placer (min.44). España reaccionó con un doble penalti-córner que no fue capaz de convertir. Quedaban 15 minutos por delante para remontar, como ya hicieron ante Alemania en la segunda fase o Bélgica, y tratar de coser su primera estrella en la camiseta. En el primer minuto del último cuarto, Calzado salvó el segundo a disparo de Groose dando una auténtica lección de reflejos. España siguió con su masterclass de hockey, combinando, presionando, pero siempre se encontró con Danneberg. A falta de a 3:46 para el desenlace, Caldas sacó al portero español del campo y dio entrada a un jugador de campo para tratar de aprovechar la superioridad. España presionaba como si no hubiera un mañana, quería hacer historia pero esta vez no hubo épica. "Yo me quedo con que hemos jugado un torneo increíble. Hemos hecho un buen partido defensivo ante Alemania, pero nos ha faltado un poco más cara a gol", reconoció Calzado, nombrado mejor portero del Mundial. "Somos un equipo muy joven que está aprendiendo a jugar este tipo de partidos. Hemos demostrado que somos un equipo muy sólido. Quedan dos años para Los Ángeles y paso a paso estaremos más cerca de conseguir las medallas allí", añadió. "Como equipo creo que merecíamos un poco más. Hemos jugado un muy buen hockey pero así es el deporte. Somos un equipo con mucha ambición y con mucho trabajo. Podemos dar muchas alegrías aún", avisó Marc Miralles.

articles.title: Hungarian Darts Trophy: Ross Smith defeats Gary Anderson as Scot's fairy-tale run ends in final
articles.summary: Ross Smith thrashed Gary Anderson 8-2 in the final of the Hungarian Darts Trophy at Budapest's MVM Dome; the 2022 European champion averaged 101 to claim a second European Tour title of the year; Anderson had survived five match darts just to reach the decider
articles.body:
Smith averaged 101 and converted 73 per cent of his attempts at a double in a near-flawless closing display at the MVM Dome, giving Anderson no way back into a contest that slipped away from the veteran almost immediately and sealing a fourth win of the day for the champion.

Smith had been the tournament's model of scoring control from the first day of his involvement, opening with a 101 average against William O'Connor that featured 116 and 112 checkouts.

He then saw off fourth seed Jonny Clayton 6-4 in the last 16 before dismantling 2023 champion Dave Chisnall 6-2 in a quarter-final that guaranteed a first-time winner of this title.

His semi-final was the most one-sided match of the weekend's business end, with last year's runner-up Danny Noppert swept aside 7-3 in a clinical display that gave Smith the fresher legs for the final.

Anderson's run, although he was vanquished in the final, ends as the story of the weekend all the same.

The two-time world champion had arrived in Budapest without a European Tour win in 2026 and opened with a statement, a 105.27 average in a 6-2 dismantling of Krzysztof Ratajski that ended the Pole's bid for back-to-back European Tour titles.

What followed was an escalating sequence of escapes.

Anderson hit eight 180s in recovering from 3-0 down to edge eighth seed Stephen Bunting in a deciding leg, then repeated the trick against second seed Gian van Veen in a quarter-final thriller.

The Scottish veteran then won the match of the tournament against Nathan Aspinall, staring down five match darts in a 7-6 epic and conjuring a 160 checkout simply to stay alive, before the final proved one test too many.

The title decider crowned a finals day of upsets that began with Aspinall knocking out Michael van Gerwen 6-4 in the last 16, recovering from 3-1 down in a match of nervy doubles to end the 2024 champion's bid for a second crown.

That came a day after top seed Luke Humphries and defending champion Niko Springer had fallen , meaning the tournament's past two winners both exited before the final session.

Aspinall's weekend, prior to meeting Anderson, was a study in finding a way through matches where he couldn't find his best form. Out-averaged by Ryan Joyce in his opening match, he came through on five 180s and sheer volume of chances at a double – and his quarter-final against Chris Dobey turned on a 156 checkout before he edged another deciding leg.

Dobey had comebacks of his own to look back on, recovering from 4-0 down to beat Tom Sykes in a decider on Saturday before closing Sunday's afternoon session by reeling in a 170 finish to see off sixth seed Josh Rock 6-3.

Dirk van Duijvenbode ended a nine-match losing run against Humphries on Saturday and was the first man into the quarter-finals, beating Rob Cross 6-4 to end the former world champion's run of successive deciding-leg escapes, before Noppert halted him 6-5.

Springer's title defence had lasted just 14 minutes against Ryan Searle on Saturday, the German missing the bull for a 164 that would have forced a decider, and with Humphries, Van Gerwen and Clayton also gone by Sunday afternoon, Van Veen stood as the highest seed left until Anderson took him out too.

articles.title: Quién es quién en los subcampeones del mundo de hockey
articles.standfirst: La media de edad está en torno a los 27 años, perfil universitario y el 60 por ciento juegan fuera
articles.summary: La media de edad está en torno a los 27 años, perfil universitario y el 60 por ciento juegan fuera
articles.body: Una veintena de chicos, de una media de edad de 27 años, surgidos en su mayoría de Barcelona, aunque también de Madrid, y con numerosos perfiles en Linkedin, señal inequívoca de que además de jugar al hockey son universitarios, se quedaron a las puertas de la conquista del mundo. Así son los subcampeones del planeta hockey, que tienen seis veces menos licencias que su oponente alemán en la final: 15.000 frente a 90.000, sumando todas las categorías. Con la ayuda de Nacho Usoz, comentarista de TVE y una figura de referencia en el hockey español, así es el grupo que ha igualado la cota más alta masculina en la historia. Portero. Juega en el Kampong de Países Bajos el campeón de la última Euroliga. Nieto de un medallista olímpico de Roma 60. Su participación fue clave para meter a España en la final con una soberbia actuación ante Paises Bajos. Es muy bueno en el uno contra uno. En el gol no pudo hacer nada. Portero. Juega en el Club de Campo. Otro que sabe lo que es ser olímpico. Es muy fiable bajo los palos y tiene una gran experiencia. Un fijo desde hace años. Centrocampista. Milita en el Real Club de Polo, tras haber vivido la experiencia de la Liga de Países Bajos. Es de los jugadores por encima de la centena de internacionalidades. Es el capitán y el organizador. La primera referencia en los penaltis córner, un apartado en el que España necesita crecer en efectividad para dominar el planeta. Defensa. Juega en el RC Polo. Ingeniero industrial. Hizo el TFG sobre el análisis de tecnologías disruptivas para la optimización del rendimiento y la gestión en el hockey profesional. Se anticipa bien, es un defensa en progresión. Centrocampista. Juega en el Canberra Chill australiano. Nieto de pionero de los 60 (Jaume Amat) y sobrino de una leyenda como Pol Amat. Se ha contagiado del rugby australiano, muy directo, rápido y físico. Sabe romper muy bien la primera presión y es clave en la conducción vertical. Defensa. Del Atlétic Terrassa. Otro de los contrastados atrás. Es polivalente, también se emplea en el centro del campo. Un gran jugador cuando hay que subir por banda. Ejercita la presión como pocos. Defensa también del Atlétic Terrassa. Otro especialista en los penaltis córner. Autor de uno de los goles ante Países Bajos. Un jugador muy hábil en los Drag-flick, las bolas por alto. Delantero. Juega en el Royal Leopold belga. Dos Juegos Olímpicos en su palmarés. Ha marcado siete goles en el Mundial, dos de ellos en la fase anterior ante Alemania y tres en la semifinal ante Países Bajos. Es un ariete de época. Delantero. Juega en el HC Rotterdam holandés. Campeón olímpico en 2016... con Argentina. Cambió de país -tenía también la nacionalidad española- por discrepancias con el cuerpo técnico. Es un jugador muy fiable. Pone la experiencia, la pausa y el último pase. Centrocampista del Club de Campo. Su tio-abuelo Jorge Solaun disputó los Juegos de Tokio 64 y México 68. Su aportación en ataque se centra en darle mucha movilidad a la delantera. Irrumpe bien desde la segunda línea. Defensa del Royal Leopold de Bélgica. Otro de los que ya contabiliza dos Juegos Olímpicos. Tiene un gran sentido de la anticipación y con más de 160 internacionalidades, el santanderino pone la experiencia en la zaga. Centrocampista. Milita en el Junior FC, de Sant Cugat. Tiene sólo 21 años, pero la experiencia de un veterano. Posee una buena técnica y gran llegada. Defensa del HC Rotterdam. Es uno de los grandes en la zaga española. Maneja bien el timing del partido, es brillante en las coberturas y maneja muy bien la salida de la bola bajo presión. Centrocampista/delantero del Oranje Rood de Países Bajos. El complemento ideal a Basterra. Un jugador con una gran habilidad para el desmarque, de gran habilidad y gran agresividad en el área. Centrocampista del Oranje Rood. Ha estudiado contabilidad financiera. Aporta ritmo, presión y equilibrio entre líneas. Tiene un gran sentido de la orientación del juego. Delantero del Oranje Rood. Es un jugador de fantasía, con un gran manejo del stick para robar arriba. Su imaginación es un plus en la selección. Tiene talento y buena llegada al área. Defensa del Den Bosch de Países Bajos. Forjado en la cantera del Atlétic Terrassa. Es un jugador muy disciplinado, que trabaja por dentro y con un gran sentido de control del ritmo. Delantero del Braxgata belga. Ataca muy bien el segundo palo y aparece en momentos decisivos del juego. Estuvo brillante en los Juegos Olímpicos de París. Defensa del Royal Uccle belga. Su padre fue medallista en los Juegos Olímpicos de Atlanta 1996. Tiene un gran físico y una gran capacidad para la presión y sostener transiciones. Delantero del RC Polo. Es un jugador con un gran presente (16 goles en la Pro League) y un futuro muy interesante. Tras pasar por el Tenis de Santander, como Alonso, recaló en el club barcelonés la temporada pasada.

articles.title: Titans release Cordell Volson, former Bengals offensive lineman
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans are releasing former Cincinnati Bengals offensive lineman Cordell Volson.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans are releasing former Cincinnati Bengals offensive lineman Cordell Volson, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

Volson was injured during training camp in 2025 and missed the entire season. He signed with the Titans in March after becoming a free agent after the season.

Volson, who turned 28 in July, didn't miss a game during his first three seasons with the Bengals, starting 48 of the 50 games in which he played. He also played in three playoff games during the 2022 postseason.

articles.title: Report: Browns moving on from preseason star wide receiver
articles.summary: Reports indicate the Browns are moving on from their preseason star Luke Floriea.
articles.body:
Roster cutdown day is never a fun day to cover the game of football. You see countless dreams and hard work fall apart, but amid all that chaos and destruction, you also see dreams come true.

In the middle of all the chaos, sadly, one fan favorite and local player will not continue his Cinderella run on the Browns .

UDFA wide receiver Floriea is being waived after a strong preseason stretch for the Browns. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler first reported the news.

The former Kent State Golden Flash was hoping to make the 53-man roster after being with the team's practice squad since last season. He dominated the preseason with six passes caught for 95 yards and an impressive three touchdowns, including one that was overturned after review.

He had a knack for getting open and finding the endzone, now Browns fans have to wait and see if he will make it back to them once again.

articles.title: Jaguars UDFA reportedly making initial 53-man roster
articles.summary: One of the Jaguars' UDFAs is reportedly making the team's initial 53-man roster after a strong preseason.
articles.body:
Jacksonville Jaguars UDFA edge rusher Bryan Thomas Jr. is reportedly making the team's initial 53-man roster, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz.

Thomas Jr. had been a standout performer during the preseason, and he capped off his impressive summer with a dominant outing in the team's preseason finale.

Against Tampa Bay, Thomas logged five pressures, according to Pro Football Focus, and he was in on three sacks.

In total over the three preseason games, Thomas Jr. logged eight pressures and four sacks. Head coach Liam Coen also noted his play against the run.

"His play style is the right way," Coen said after the final preseason game. "It fits a lot of the things that we preach and that we're about as a team. When you have a gift of rushing the passer, man, it's something that you can't ignore. I thought he did some nice things against the run as well tonight. I thought the defense as a whole, obviously with the shutout, was huge, being led by Bryan. He's making it really difficult, which is a good thing. It's just what we're hunting up. He's had that skill set. That was something we really appreciated about his game. He's just continued to do it on this stage."

In a crowded defensive end room, Thomas Jr. faced an uphill battle when it came to making the final roster, but his steady production and regular flashes helped him stand out.

Fellow defensive ends Danny Striggow and BJ Green each made the Jaguars ' 53-man roster last year as UDFAs.

articles.title: Bears expected to waive top undrafted free agent offensive lineman
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears are expected to part ways with undrafted free agent guard Caden Barnett amid roster cuts.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears are expected to waive undrafted free agent offensive lineman Caden Barnett, according to Chicago Tribune's Brad Biggs .

Barnett, who played both guard and tackle at Wyoming, worked exclusively at right guard with Chicago this summer, and he was contending with fellow guards Jordan McFadden and Luke Newman, who are both expected to earn a roster spot.

Biggs noted that Barnett, who received $277,500 guaranteed when he initially signed, is strongly expected to re-sign to the practice squad.

articles.title: Denver Broncos have waived cornerback Brent Austin
articles.summary: According to Mike Klis of 9News, the Denver Broncos have waived cornerback Brent Austin.
articles.body:
According to Mike Klis of 9News, the Denver Broncos have waived cornerback Brent Austin today.

Austin was an undrafted rookie free agent cornerback who started at James Madison before transferring to USF. He ended up finishing his college career with two seasons at Cal. That season he posted forty-two tackles and thirteen pass deflections. He is a guy we viewed as a developmental candidate on the practice squad as rookie:

All things considered, it seems most realistic that Austin will have a good shot at earning a spot on the practice squad for continued development. You can never have enough quality cover players, and Austin's collegiate tape and resume show a promising player who has the ability to contribute as a reserve player in the future.

He had a great training camp as an undrafted rookie, but the cornerback position is a stacked one in Denver. I would look for him to be a priority addition to the practice squad based on what little we've gotten from camp reports.

articles.title: Report: Saints made their decision about this year's starting kicker
articles.summary: The New Orleans Saints have been all over the place with kickers since trading Wil Lutz, and now, 2026 will be opened by a different starter again.
articles.body:
Over the course of the New Orleans Saints ' 58 seasons of existence, they have had 37 different kickers attempt at least one kick during a regular-season game. One of the most notable during that time frame was Wil Lutz, holding down the fort for seven seasons before being traded to the Denver Broncos .

Since then, the Saints have utilized two options, Blake Grupe and Charlie Smyth, who both had their bright spots and low moments. Now, Smyth was let go before the NFL roster cuts deadline ( but could return on the practice squad ). For 2026, they will rely on another option, though, as recently signed two-time All-Pro Daniel Carlson will take the reins to open the season, as was reported by Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football .

Carlson was picked up before the third preseason game for New Orleans, and in that third matchup, he had three kicking attempts, making two field goals and an extra point, including a 53-yard bomb that likely won him the job. After spotty performances from Smyth and Tanner Brown this summer, Carlson will step in and earn a starting job for his ninth consecutive season.

articles.title: Serie A | Napoli 1-2 Como: Fabregas earns big victory at the Maradona
articles.summary: Como pounced on defensive errors to secure a big 2-1 victory away to Napoli in an early challenge for top four spots, as Martin Baturina and Tasos Douvikas w...
articles.body:
Como pounced on defensive errors to secure a big 2-1 victory away to Napoli in an early challenge for top four spots, as Martin Baturina and Tasos Douvikas were on target.

The Partenopei made two changes from the side that beat Genoa 2-0, with Matias Olivera and surprisingly Noa Lang replacing Leonardo Spinazzola and Alisson Santos, as the winger had been transfer-listed. Kevin De Bruyne was still only fit for the bench, with Alessandro Buongiorno and Luca Marianucci injured. Como opened their season with a 1-1 home draw against Udinese, again starting summer signings Trevoh Chalobah, Yan Couto, Bruno Kaiki and Luis Milla.

There was a hug before kick-off between coaches Max Allegri and Cesc Fabregas, who famously clashed on the touchline and in the press room last season.

NAPLES, ITALY – AUGUST 30: Massimiliano Allegri, Manager of Napoli and Cesc Fabregas, Manager of Como interact before the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Como 1907 at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on August 30, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)

Como kept possession early doors, but Olivera pulled back from the by-line for a mad scramble in the six-yard box that Andre Frank Zambo Anguissa and Scott McTominay couldn't finish off.

Lucas Da Cunha's strike was deflected wide and Alex Valle couldn't keep the header on target from the resulting corner, but Como found the breakthrough on 16 minutes.

Assane Diao got away from Olivera down the right and rolled across for Martin Baturina, who in one sweeping movement turned around to drill into the near bottom corner from 12 yards.

NAPLES, ITALY – AUGUST 30: Martin Baturina of Como celebrates scoring his team's first goal with teammates during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Como 1907 at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on August 30, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)

Lang really should've equalised moments later, but he turned a free header inches over from the Matteo Politano cross, then Como wasted a golden opportunity on the counter-attack with five on three, trying to walk it into the net.

That proved costly, because Napoli got the equaliser a minute later as Hojlund gathered on the edge of the area and turned to fire through a sea of legs into the bottom corner.

NAPLES, ITALY – AUGUST 30: Rasmus Hojlund of Napoli celebrates scoring his team's first goal with coaching staff during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Como 1907 at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on August 30, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)

However, Anguissa got into a terrible tangle playing out from the back with a poor back-pass to Amir Rrahmani, intercepted by Baturina to set up the easy Tasos Douvikas finish inside the area.

Yan Couto got back for a great tackle on Hojlund, then saw penalty appeals rejected for a nudge on Lang, but Como had two big opportunities in first half stoppages.

NAPLES, ITALY – AUGUST 30: Martin Baturina of Como is challenged by Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa of Napoli during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Como 1907 at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on August 30, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)

Alex Meret flew to fingertip the Baturina header over, but on the resulting corner was fortunate that the Nico Paz header squirmed under his body, getting trapped before rolling over the line.

Como continued to dominate possession and the initiative after the restart, although Olivera volleyed wide on a rare counter-attack, so Allegri introduced Kevin De Bruyne, Alisson Santos and Leonardo Spinazzola.

NAPLES, ITALY – AUGUST 30: Scott McTominay of Napoli is challenged by Lucas Da Cunha of Como during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Como 1907 at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on August 30, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)

This prompted a period of pressure and possession from the hosts, but Butez was quick off his line to anticipate Hojlund, then Ivan Smolcic showed brave defending to stop De Bruyne nodding in the Stanislav Lobotka cross, leading to a nasty clash of heads.

De Bruyne and Alisson Santos also had efforts inches off target, then Marc-Oliver Kempf off balance had to scramble a De Bruyne assist clear from the six-yard box. Lorenzo Lucca and Douvikas had headers straight at the respective goalkeepers in stoppages.

Lobotka did have the ball in the net at the 95th minute, but play had already been halted for Lucca's offside position in the build-up.

For Rose, it marked the fourth ace in his PGA Tour career. Perhaps his most famous came while playing at the Rio Olympics in 2016.

articles.title: Patriots placing top backup swing tackle on injured reserve
articles.summary: The Patriots are reportedly placing improved second-year offensive tackle Marcus Bryant on injured reserve.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots are reportedly placing second-year offensive tackle Marcus Bryant on injured reserve, according to ESPN's Mike Reiss on Sunday.

Bryant shot up the depth chart as the Patriots ' projected top swing tackle in training camp. The former seventh-round draft pick out of Missouri had worked hard to carve out a real role on the roster.

But it was ultimately halted by the injury that he sustained in the Week 2 preseason matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles .

NFL teams have two designated return spots when placing players on injured reserve. So Bryant could return after missing at least the first four games of the season. Bryant being out would now mean that rookie first-round draft pick Caleb Lomu would project as the Patriots' top backup swing tackle.

Lomu has played at both spots in training camp, but he has predominantly worked at right tackle behind veteran Morgan Moses. It has been an up-and-down summer for the former University of Utah standout, and now, he is one injury away from being thrown into the fire in his first NFL season.

articles.title: Ben Johnson and Bears get bad news in NFL analyst's take
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears won't like this hot take on their situation.
articles.body:
Ben Johnson has already worked wonders with the Chicago Bears . There's really no reason to believe this team isn't destined for something great after rounding out the season first place in the NFC North last year.

But, it's not perfect in the Windy City. Johnson, of course, has some stuff to work out before the season really gets rolling. The sooner he does it, the better for all involved.

Josh Edwards of CBS Sports has a feature out on Thursday naming one position each NFL team should look at before the roster deadline has passed.

For Chicago, he wants to see this team work on its secondary. It makes sense, because the team's secondary has been under attack, literally, as of late, when it comes to injuries.

"The secondary has been decimated by injury this summer," he says in the piece. "Safety Coby Bryant will miss an extended period of time and Kyler Gordon, Elijah Hicks and Jaylon Jones have all been watching practice from the sideline."

He adds, "Having said all of that, head coach Ben Johnson may just decide to add another tight end."

The secondary is often a part of the lineup that gets overlooked. But, Johnson isn't the kind of guy to overlook anything. He's very calculated in how he approaches this team and its talent. Either way, don't be surprised if you see Johnson make some bold additions before the roster deadline, and one of those could be the secondary.

articles.title: NFL roster cuts: Arizona Cardinals reportedly cut CB Sean Murphy-Bunting
articles.summary: The Cardinals are cutting ties with a veteran CB with 65 career starts and $1.75 million in guaranteed salary.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals have many cuts to make before 3 p.m. Arizona time. One reported cut is a surprise.

According to Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports , the Cardinals are cutting veteran cornerback Sean Murphy-Bunting.

The move is surprising because has $1.75 million of his scheduled $2.39 million guaranteed. He has 65 career starts and can play both inside and outside. He worked as the Cardinals' starting nickel corner all offseason while Garrett Williams has recovered from a torn Achilles.

This move suggests that the Cardinals are confident that Williams will be able to play in Week 1, and perhaps they will keep Kalen King, who had been working as the No. 2 nickelback all offseason.

Because Murphy-Bunting is a vested veteran, he will not have to go through waivers. He might be a practice squad candidate as a result, and he will still get his guaranteed salary.

Murphy-Bunting was entering his third season with the Cardinals after signing a three-year contract in free agency. Last season, he did not play, suffering a knee injury in the offseason.

The Cardinals will announce their cuts after making the necessary moves to get to 53 players on the roster by 3 p.m. Arizona time.

articles.title: Why Man Utd goal was allowed to stand - despite Maguire 'handball'
articles.summary: The handball law often serves to confuse supporters - and it reared its head again as Harry Maguire celebrated putting Manchester United in front against Ips...
articles.body:
The handball law often serves to confuse supporters - and it reared its head again as Harry Maguire celebrated putting Manchester United in front against Ipswich Town.

The ball came off the United defender's arm, before he then moved a few yards forward into the box and his shot found its way into the back of the net.

Surely the goal would be ruled out. After all, any handball by the scorer means the goal must be disallowed.

Apart from one very important point - Maguire did not actually score the goal.

Maguire's effort was going well wide, and deflected into the back of the net off Jacob Greaves. It was officially an own goal.

There are three exemptions for when accidental handball by the scorer does not count:

Action of a defender results in an own goal

The video assistant referee Jarred Gillett said to referee Craig Pawson: "It's an own goal and the accidental handball is not punishable, so we recommend you award the goal."

Indeed, the goal could have been disallowed had the VAR felt it was deliberate handball by Maguire.

Manchester United went on to win the game 5-2 thanks to a Bruno Fernandes hat-trick.

It is rare but we saw a similar situation in January 2023 with a goal for Brentford against Liverpool.

The ball accidentally came off the arm of Ben Mee and ended up in the back of the net, but it was not going towards goal and deflected off Ibrahima Konate for an own goal.

Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil told Sky Sports that it is "tough for a referee" to judge on what is a "complicated rule".

Former England goalkeeper Paul Robinson, speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live, also had some sympathy for the officials.

"Once again we are victims of the law," said Robinson. "You can't criticise the VAR officials because they are enforcing the law that they are given.

"They train extremely hard, they learn their profession but it was a handball and Harry Maguire who struck the shot.

"Thankfully that wasn't a game-defining goal. How many times has the handball law been changed?"

Ex-Ipswich forward and Sky Sports pundit Darren Bent added: "It's one of those rules where I understand because it's there in black and white, but it still doesn't feel right.

"Harry Maguire directly impacts what happens to the ball and it ends up in the back of the net at a crucial time for Ipswich. If it hits your hand and he is the one that directly impacts it, it's not a nice one to take."

articles.title: Tennessee Titans parting ways with Will Levis
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans announced on Sunday that they are placing quarterback Will Levis on waivers as part of roster cuts.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans had a serious quarterback battle during training camp and preseason. Cam Ward is the undeniable starter, but behind him, a battle raged for who would back him up. The Titans brought in Mitch Trubisky and Hendon Hooker to compete with incumbent backup Will Levis. Today, as roster cuts are pouring in ahead of the 5:00 p.m. CST deadline to trim rosters down to 53-men, the Titans announced they are waiving Levis.

Levis was drafted by the Titans in 2023 and replaced Ryan Tannehill in Mike Vrabel's final season as head coach. Through the 2023 and 2024 seasons, Levis appeared in 21 games and completed 339 passes for 3,899 yards and 21 touchdowns. He also threw 16 interceptions and took 69 sacks, averaging a quarterback rating of 82.7.

He sat out the 2025 season after undergoing shoulder surgery during the offseason and had hopes of regaining some playing time in 2026. The Titans, though, have been open to trading Levis for a while, and since that hasn't happened, the Titans have decided to part ways with their former second-round draft pick.

With Levis on Waivers, the Titans are eating $3 million in dead cap space ($2 million in cash) if he goes unclaimed . They paid him a $906,000 bonus at the start of training camp, and his $1.1 million salary is guaranteed.

Without Levis, Trubisky and Hooker will be on the roster to back up Cam Ward in 2026.

articles.title: '14,000 runs for a reason' - Root calm on form
articles.summary: Joe Root is “not too concerned” about his modest returns with the bat, saying he has “14,000 runs for a reason”.
articles.body:
Joe Root is "not too concerned" about his modest returns with the bat, saying he has "14,000 runs for a reason".

Captain Root, England's all-time leading Test run-scorer, has passed 50 only twice this summer. An average of 29.44 is his second-lowest in a home season in a 14-year international career.

The 35-year-old has been lbw nine times in his past seven Tests, including on seven occasions this summer.

But Root pointed to the challenge faced by all batters against the moving ball in the UK this summer and his own remarkable Test career. Only India great Sachin Tendulkar has more than the Yorkshireman's 14,208 runs.

"I've played this game a long time and I've always found ways of solving those problems and working it through," Root told the BBC's Today at the Test. "I don't see this as being any different.

"There's a reason why I've got 14,000 runs and a reason why I've played the best part of 15 years at this level.

"Of course it's frustrating that there's sort of a trend. There are probably four umpires' calls within that, which could have gone the other way, and the ball is probably deviating more than it ever has.

"You try and be realistic and understand where everything's at, but also be aware of what you need to do to keep improving and keep getting better. I'm pretty sure I'll get through the other side. I'm not too concerned about that."

Last summer, former Australia opener David Warner took a dig at Root's prospects of success in the Ashes series that was to follow when he said: "He will have to take the surfboard off his front leg."

At the time, Warner's suggestion Root had an lbw problem was incorrect. In a run that began in August 2022 and ended with the fourth Ashes Test in Melbourne in December, Root was lbw to seam bowlers in Test cricket on only three occasions.

However, Root's recent run of leg-before dismissals began when he was trapped by Australia's Jhye Richardson in the second innings of the Boxing Day Test. Since then he has been lbw nine times in 12 innings, all to pace bowlers.

Root's specific problem has been against right-arm bowlers, pitching the ball outside off stump and nipping it back towards him.

Of the nine dismissals in his run of lbws, none have come at the hands of bowlers with high pace, rather those with a maximum speed of around 84mph.

"You're never given anything in this game," said Root. "You have to work for everything. You have to keep working hard and I'll certainly keep doing that.

"You're constantly going to get challenged and you're constantly going to have to look to evolve and learn, but that's never been something I've shied away from and I certainly won't be doing moving forward."

Root was backed to solve the lbw issue by former England captain Michael Vaughan, who said: "He's always overcome problems and I'm pretty sure he'll overcome this one.

"It is an issue because it's happening on a regular basis but he's had issues in the past that he's managed to come back from. There's no question he'll be fine in time."

Despite no big contribution from the captain, England sealed a series win over Pakistan with a 194-run win in the second Test at Lord's.

It gave Root a second win in as many matches at the beginning of his second spell as skipper, and England their first series win since 2024.

The build-up to the second Test was dominated by the controversy surrounding England pace bowler Brydon Carse, who was dropped from the squad because of an incident outside a nightclub in Derby.

On Tuesday, Root said he was "hacked off" to be dealing with another drinking issue involving an England player and confirmed he had addressed his squad to warn them against a repeat.

On Sunday, Root said he wanted his players to celebrate the win at Lord's "sensibly".

"It's important that we're not talking about that, absolutely," said Root. "It's hard to win Test matches, it's hard to win Test series.

"Enjoy it and celebrate it, but in a sensible and grown-up way."

And Vaughan suggested the England squad should "stay in".

"Have a quiet one," he said. "I don't want to be picking up the paper tomorrow morning or mid-afternoon on social media and seeing a few clicks. You've won a good series, just have a quiet night."
authors: Stephan Shemilt - Cricket Correspondent at Lord's

articles.title: Does USC's poor opening game attendance mean Lincoln Riley's on the hot seat already?
articles.summary: USC's sparse crowd against San Jose State sparked roasts, but attendance history shows even playoff-bound teams struggle with noon kickoffs and heat.
articles.body: The 2026 college football season is officially underway, and with it returns one of the greatest sporting traditions: criticizing crowd sizes and attendance. This season, the culprit was USC, as the Trojans opened their 2026 season at home against San Jose State. Because college football scheduling is no longer based on what makes sense given a location, local time zones, time of year, or weather, NBC picked the 12pm Pacific Time window for kickoff. That's always a tough time for Southern California locals, because Saturday traffic in the Los Angeles area, particularly for events around downtown LA, makes getting in and out of venues an hours-long slog. Combine it with the $60 parking a mile away, a poor quality opponent, and one of the most brutal weather days of the year, with atrocious heat and humidity, and it's a recipe for reduced attendance. USC FOOTBALL RIPPED FOR PATHETIC CROWD AT HOME OPENER: 'ABSOLUTELY EMBARRASSING' That's exactly what happened. And the college football world rushed to do what it does best, roast other programs. The crowd at kickoff was extremely small, though, it did fill in a bit more by late in the first quarter. Unsurprisingly, with the game already decided in the first 15-18 minutes and the awful conditions, it quickly emptied out. Many commentators rushed to say that the low turnout is why USC will not make the College Football Playoff this year, while adding that Lincoln Riley is officially on the hot seat. And to be fair to those uninformed opinions, there's little doubt that USC's underwhelming performances in recent years contributed to the poor showing. But one thing those commentators, and most fans, completely misunderstand, is that attendance and fan support has quite literally nothing to do with team quality. This phenomenon though, continues to have widespread support across college football. Fans show up to watch Arkansas on seven days a year, therefore Arkansas must be a good program with good players. Does it matter if the Razorbacks finish 2-10? Does that make them a bad program? Apparently not, because their fans showed up to watch them lose. Then there's the other, oft-ignored part of this discussion: fan attendance at big programs in hot weather in the heat has often been a problem. Here's how one story covering the Florida Gators' struggles to fill up their stadium for noon kickoffs described "The Swamp." "As I enter the stadium a few minutes before kickoff, the audio system rumbles through the cement pillars and I’m ready for an overwhelming surge of energy. But when I make it out into the open air, the first thing I notice are empty metal bleachers reflecting rays of bright Florida sun. While the alumni section I’m standing in is filled, the top third of the student section opposite me is mostly empty, a scatter-plot weighted toward the bottom. I was expecting the frenzied vibe of a rave; what I’ve got is more of a buzzy mimosa brunch." And that was a highly attended game, according to Tyler Nettuno, a reporter for the school paper explained. "The general admission seats above both end zones are patchy, too. 'For a 12 o’clock game,' Nettuno continues, 'this is the best I’ve seen it.'" The story goes on to point out that "Ohio State, Virginia Tech and Ole Miss suffered declines of greater than 5%" in attendance. As well as the fact that Clemson didn't sell out a single game in a year they won a National Championship. While Ohio State fans explained they'd rather go sit at a bar with friends or at home instead of watching a blowout win over Florida Atlantic. In 2025, crowd shots of a mostly empty "Death Valley" at LSU went viral on college football Twitter. Attendance has little to do with whether a team is headed for a playoff spot. And the reasons behind the national decline in attendance are obvious. It's easier than ever to watch games through streaming services on phones. Ticket prices continue to increase, even as everyday life becomes increasingly expensive. Staying home in bad weather allows fans to track other games instead of being in miserable heat to watch a blowout win. Many younger alumni aren't as dedicated to football either, as schools bolster their academic admission standards or push for more STEM students. Not to mention that we ran this experiment, on how much crowds impact outcomes in home games during COVID, and found that, at least in the NFL, league average home field advantage essentially stayed almost identical from 2019-2020. Fans and fan noise just don't matter as much as they'd like to believe. OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD So with that established, did the Trojans 42-26 win over San Jose State tell us anything about their hopes of reaching the College Football Playoff? No, not really. Opposing fans ready to bury USC and Riley, particularly the ever-disgruntled Oklahoma fans, jumped all over the poor fourth quarter performance. And justifiably so. But when USC's starters were in the game, they dominated. In the first half, for example, San Jose State had five drives. On four of them, the Spartans gained a total of 36 yards. Their first quarter "offense" was six plays for 11 yards and two punts. They did have one drive go 66 yards on 14 plays before a turnover on downs. But overall, their offense averaged just 3.9 yards per play and gained 102 total yards. Their first drive of the third quarter was a three-and-out with six yards. So while the starters and second string were in the game, SJSU gained 108 yards on 29 plays. To their credit, the Spartans were able to move the ball against the Trojans' backups and third stringers, with plenty of USC's players held out entirely due to injury concerns. But for those quick to bury them for 2026, we can look at some recent history to show that isn't warranted. They needed their starters to score a final touchdown with five minutes left to win 24-14 as 45.5 point favorites. They made the playoff at the end of that season. In 2025, the eventual SEC champion Georgia Bulldogs had a two possession lead over FCS team Austin Peay until midway through the fourth quarter, leaving their starters in before securing an unimpressive 28-6 win as 48.5 point favorites. Also in 2025, eventual undefeated national champions Indiana beat Old Dominion 27-14 in week one and allowed 218 rushing yards and 314 total yards with nearly seven yards per play. They were 24-point favorites. So are there reasons for concern around USC? Sure, the backups will be needed throughout the season, and the poor fourth quarter wasn't encouraging. Riley hasn't exactly given fans reasons for confidence at SC, and it's clear that their secondary needs work. But Jayden Maiava was 25/29 for 286 yards and two touchdowns without playing a particularly impressive game, by his standards. articles.title: From FSU to Dan Mullen, here are three 'overreactions' from week zero of the college football season
articles.summary: Florida State struggled against New Mexico State, UNLV fell to Memphis, and USC's empty Coliseum sparked heated debate in a wild week zero opener.
articles.body: The college football appetizer known as week zero has come and gone, and although it wasn't quite as robust as the real opening week that is still to come, it did more than enough to keep football fans satisfied while they wait for the main course this coming Saturday. Yesterday felt like a return to normalcy for college football fanatics after months of court dates and NIL doomsday prophecies, and it was nice to just sit back and watch some glorious pigskin action without worrying about any of that extracurricular garbage that has been plaguing the news cycle. One of the telltale signs that the season is underway is the myriad overreactions you will see up and down your social media timeline, and Saturday evening/Sunday morning was no different. NFL TO NCAA? COURTROOM CHAOS IS GIVING PRO ATHLETES A BIZARRE PATH BACK TO COLLEGE, AND IT'S ONLY JUST BEGUN As you'll see, it's never too early to overreact to your team's performance in the first week of the year, even with an expanded College Football Playoff affording teams more regular-season Mulligans than ever before. Here are three overreactions you'll see all over your phone screen as you do your Sunday afternoon scroll, and some carry more weight than others. Florida State will be lucky to win three games this year If I could sum up Florida State's 2026 opener against New Mexico State on Saturday night in one word, it would be "woof." And I'm not alone in that assessment, FSU fans took to social media for the majority of the past 16 hours and absolutely trashed their beloved Noles. COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S AP TOP 25 IS OUT: WHO’S OVERRATED, UNDERRATED AND FLAT-OUT SNUBBED? It wasn't without merit, either. The Seminoles were 31.5-point favorites heading into the contest, with New Mexico State coming off a 4-8 season in 2025. Florida State ended up only winning by 17, and the game got as close as 10 midway through the fourth quarter. If it wasn't for a bad pick in the red zone to open the game and a drop by a wide open receiver in the end zone, the Aggies might have actually pulled the upset in Tallahassee. FIVE COLLEGE FOOTBALL TEAMS RANKED OUTSIDE THE PRESEASON TOP-10 THAT WENT ON TO WIN IT ALL The Noles got bullied on the lines of scrimmage by a team much smaller than them and their new quarterback, Auburn transfer Ashton Daniels, was a mixed bag in his debut in garnet and gold. Fans are already calling for head coach Mike Norvell's firing, but the odds of that happening before the season are slim given his exorbitant buyout. The truth is, FSU supporters might be in for another long season, and this overreaction might carry some weight. It might be time to pull the plug on the Dan Mullen Experiment The UNLV Rebels were a trendy pick to make the College Football Playoff this season as a Group of 6 representative, and while that might still happen, those dreams took a big hit with a 27-21 home loss to fellow G6 Playoff hopefuls Memphis on Saturday. Head coach Dan Mullen spent the majority of the news conference complaining that his fans were making too much noise while the Rebs were on offense instead of worrying about other things like why his defense was getting torched by a Division II transfer at quarterback. I've seen a ton of UNLV fans making impassioned pleas to Mullen asking him to fire defensive coordinator Paul Guenther, but plenty of them have come to the realization that it won't be happening. As a Florida Gator fan, I can confirm Mullen is prepared to go down with the ship as his embattled DC sits right alongside him in the captain's quarters. This is the fatal flaw of Mullen: he's stubborn and loyal to a fault. He had a ton of chances to fire Florida defensive coordinator Todd Grantham as he harpooned any chances the Gators had of winning a championship in 2020, and I fear he will do much of the same in Vegas. Now, the part that makes this an overreaction is the fact that Guenther is in year one as the UNLV defensive coordinator. Perhaps he turns it around, but getting dissected by a quarterback and head coach (Charles Huff) in their very first game with the program is not exactly a good sign. File this one under "something to keep an eye on." USC fans have given up on Lincoln Riley in a pivotal year If you were on social media at all in the last 24 hours, you are probably aware of USC's attendance problem during their opening game against San Jose State. The Trojans have arguably their most talented team since head coach Lincoln Riley arrived five seasons ago and have a legitimate shot at making the CFP, but the fans weren't convinced. Several shots of the Coliseum showed what could, generously, be described as a half empty stadium. So what gives? Defenders of the program will blame the empty seats on things like a heat wave, or classes not starting yet. Others fire back with screenshots of a home venue packed to the gills with USC fans during similarly hot temperatures just a few short years ago. Are fans punting on Riley right as he's about to turn things around? I think the truth is probably a lot more simple and less sinister than that. Los Angeles isn't a huge sports town, and I think fans need to see proof of concept before they show up to a game and support their team. I say this as someone who is from a similarly fair-weather sports town in Miami; the Dolphins and Hurricanes will play to a stadium that is barely half full unless they are legitimate championship contenders. It's just the way it is. I will say this, for as empty as the Coliseum was on Saturday, the students did their part, as their section of the stadium was packed to the gills and screaming full throat for their Trojans. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP This is absolutely an "overreaction," and the minute USC is 4-0 and ranked in the top 10 when they play Oregon, I guarantee you that the building will be rocking.

articles.title: Kelani Jordan Shocks Kendal Grey to Win NXT Women's Title at Heatwave 2026
articles.summary: Kelani Jordan defeated Kendal Grey at Heatwave on Sunday to win her first NXT Women's Championship.
articles.body:
Kelani Jordan defeated Kendal Grey at Heatwave on Sunday to win her first NXT Women's Championship.

After months and even years of lobbying for a one-on-one opportunity at the NXT women's title, Jordan finally got it on Sunday in what was Grey's first title defense at a premium live event.

Grey became NXT women's champion for the first time in June when she beat Lola Vice at the Great American Bash.

In order to earn that title shot in the first place, Grey defeated Jordan in a No. 1 contender's match, allowing her to exact some revenge against Kelani for a loss back in May.

Coming out of Great American Bash, Grey had a successful title defense against Nattie, and also beat Vice in an NXT Underground match on NXT TV.

After that, Jordan threw her name into the mix for a chance at the NXT Women's Championship once again, and thanks to her desire to prove she was a fighting champion, Grey quickly agreed to give Jordan a title bout.

Grey told Jordan she could have her championship match whenever she wanted it, prompting the former women's North American champion and TNA Knockouts world champion to choose Heatwave.

Leading up to Heatwave, Jordan gained some major momentum when she teamed with another NXT Women's Championship hopeful in Kali Armstrong.

Jordan and Armstrong teamed up to beat Grey and Wren Sinclair on the Aug. 18 episode of NXT, allowing Kelani to enter Heatwave on a positive note.

Kelani continued her winning ways at Heatwave, beating Grey to become NXT women's champion for the first time in her career.

articles.title: Grayson Waller Wins NXT Title vs. Zilla Fatu, Cruz Montana, Tony D'Angelo at Heatwave 2026
articles.summary: Grayson Waller beat Tony D'Angelo, Cruz Montana and Zilla Fatu in a Fatal 4-Way match at Heatwave on Sunday to win the NXT Championship.
articles.body:
Grayson Waller beat Tony D'Angelo, Cruz Montana and Zilla Fatu in a Fatal 4-Way match at Heatwave on Sunday to win the NXT Championship.

Montana appeared to have the win in hand before Waller snuck in to steal the victory, winning his first career singles title in WWE.

For about a month leading up to Heatwave, D'Angelo became a target for several members of the NXT roster, including Montana, who made his official debut as an NXT Superstar on the July 21 episode of NXT.

After D'Angelo's successful title defense against Naraku, Montana arrived in NXT and immediately made it clear that he was coming for D'Angelo and the NXT title.

One week later, Waller made a surprise appearance on NXT TV despite having been part of the WWE roster for years.

Waller cut a scathing promo on the NXT locker room and took shots at several individual talents, including D'Angelo and Montana.

With both Montana and Waller vying for an NXT Championship opportunity, D'Angelo agreed to put the title on the line against the winner of a No. 1 contender match between them.

On the Aug. 11 episode of NXT, Montana and Waller fought to what was essentially a no contest, as Fatu made his surprise WWE debut by interrupting the match and attacking both Superstars.

D'Angelo was on commentary for the match, and Zilla turned his attention to Tony D as the show went off the air, establishing that he too wanted to become NXT champion.

The next week on NXT, general manager Robert Stone announced that D'Angelo would defend the NXT Championship against Montana and Waller in a Triple Threat match at Heatwave, but that didn't last for long.

Later in the night, Stone held a contract signing for Fatu, and revealed that Fatu's first match in NXT would be for the NXT title. Zilla then announced that he was being added to the title match at Heatwave to make it a Fatal 4-Way.

It didn't take long for Waller to ascend to the top of NXT, as he was victorious Sunday in his first premium live event match since rejoining the brand, allowing him to become NXT champion in the process.

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr. makes Giants’ roster, and No. 13 is available
articles.summary: OBJ is back in NYC. Officially. Odell Beckham Jr. made the Giants‘ 53-man roster on the NFL’s cutdown day Sunday, kickstarting a second chapter with the orga...
articles.body:
Odell Beckham Jr . made the Giants ' 53-man roster on the NFL's cutdown day Sunday, kickstarting a second chapter with the organization where he became a star as a first-round pick out of LSU in 2014.

The team also waived 2023 third-round pick Jalin Hyatt, who wears jersey No. 13. So it won't be long until Beckham ditches his recent No. 3 for the number he made famous.

Beckham, 33, signed in the spring and reunited with John Harbaugh, who coached him in Baltimore in 2023. Then OBJ had a strong preseason and training camp to cement his spot on the Giants team that will take the field Sept. 13 against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 1.

"I'm excited," Beckham told NFL insider Josina Anderson Sunday after practice. "I found out when I was walking off the field. Coach said, 'Congratulations,' and he said that I worked hard. I told him I will give him everything I got. He said, 'Let's go do it.'"

Beckham made 390 catches for 5,476 yards and 44 touchdowns for the Giants in five seasons from 2014-2018.

Former GM Dave Gettleman paid Beckham a 5-year, $90 million contract in Aug. 2018 and then traded him to the Cleveland Browns in March 2019.

Once Beckham escaped toxic Cleveland, he helped the L.A. Rams win a Super Bowl in 2021, tearing his ACL in the game.

The mounting injuries kept OBJ out of football in 2022. But he rebounded in Baltimore, had a cup of coffee last season with the Miami Dolphins and then resolved to give a triumphant Giant return one more go.

Beckham told Anderson that quarterbacks Jameis Winston and Jaxson Dart both showed love to him after he officially made the team Sunday.

"Now I just got to go get it," Beckham said. "I have one more gear to go, one more gear in me. I came to New York to give my all, and that's what they're going to get out of me. To the city, to the fans: I love you."

Beckham makes a receiving corps that also includes Malik Nabers, rookie third-round pick Malachi Fields and veterans Darnell Mooney and Darius Slayton.

Braxton Berrios was released, but the Giants intend to bring him back for Week 1, as well. Calvin Austin had been playing well all preseason but tore his right ACL in the final week of camp.

Now the Giants' efforts with Beckham should turn to developing more chemistry with Dart.

The starting quarterback and Beckham did not connect much in July or August. Beckham did more damage while playing with Winston.

Dart will be the one playing in the games, so that should be the Harbaugh's next step to get the best out of a physically resurgent Beckham.

The Giants' cuts on Saturday included four of the team's draft picks between 2022 and 2024: offensive lineman Evan Neal, Hyatt, running back Eric Gray and linebacker Darius Muasau.

Neal was the No. 7 overall pick in the first round of the 2022 draft. Hyatt was a third-round pick in 2023, and Gray went two rounds later the same year. Muasau was a sixth-rounder in 2024.

The Giants now have only four of their 18 draft picks from the 2022 and 2023 NFL Drafts still on their roster: Kayvon Thibodeaux, Micah McFadden, Deonte Banks and John Michael Schmitz.

Elsewhere on the roster, center Bryan Hudson made the team over veteran Lucas Patrick as Schmitz's backup. And 2025 seventh-round tight end Thomas Fidone made the initial roster after catching everything thrown his way all camp.

Corner Nic Jones, safety Elijah Campbell and linebacker Zaire Barnes made the team as core special teamers.

Harbaugh interestingly practiced his team prior to making cuts on Sunday, an unorthodox decision that guarantees players are healthy enough to take the field the day they're released.

They'll be back on the field in New Jersey Monday through Wednesday. Then they'll have a break before revving back up for Dallas.
authors: Pat Leonard, New York Daily News

articles.title: Here's who made the New England Patriots roster this season

articles.body:
The New England Patriots roster should feel different this season.

Drake Maye established himself as an MVP candidate last year. Splashes in free agency and the trade market surrounded the quarterback with talent that was lacking in key spots. The end of the roster might've had some shuffling, but the important pieces for New England were penciled in long ago.

AJ Brown and Romeo Doubs were always going to be the 1-2 in New England's receiving corps. Trading Kayshon Boutte to the Texans solved the only true question of the offseason. New England opted to carry six receivers on its 53-man roster with Pop Douglas, Mack Hollins, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III completing the group.

Alijah Vera-Tucker and Caleb Lomu were the top additions to the offensive line as the former slips into a starting role at right guard. Lomu, New England's first-round pick, is the top swing tackle should Will Campbell or Morgan Moses miss time.

Christian Gonzalez returns, without a new contract, as New England's top cornerback. He reached his potential last year and leads a secondary that signed Kevin Byard to a one-year deal. Christian Barmore, Milton Williams and Robert Spillane are among key returnees with Gonzalez.

It's a roster that has more high-end talent than a year ago. Depth at linebacker, defensive end and guard is lacking, but New England is in a better place than it was a year ago.

articles.title: Underdog WR Tay Martin Learns Detroit Lions 53-Man Roster Fate
articles.summary: Wide receiver Tay Martin has earned a spot on the Detroit Lions’ initial 53-man roster following an impressive training camp and preseason.
articles.body:
Tay Martin's push for a roster spot has officially paid off.

The Detroit Lions are keeping Martin on their initial 53-man roster, according to Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News , completing an impressive climb for a receiver who entered training camp fighting for one of the final jobs in a crowded position group.

Martin did not simply survive the competition. He earned his way onto the team.

Martin Took Advantage of His Opportunity

Detroit entered camp with Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams and Isaac TeSlaa established at the top of the receiver room, leaving Martin among a large group battling for the remaining openings.

By mid-August, the Lions themselves were calling the competition an "all-out" battle , with Martin continuing to distinguish himself as a receiver, blocker and special-teams contributor.

His case only became stronger down the stretch. Martin caught four passes and a touchdown in Saturday's 25-16 preseason victory over the Indianapolis Colts , giving the coaching staff one final reminder of what he could offer before roster decisions were due.

We had already identified Martin as a serious contender for Detroit's final receiver spot before the preseason concluded.

The news becomes even more significant after Detroit's decision earlier Sunday to release veteran Greg Dortch , who had spent much of camp looking like a strong candidate for the No. 4 receiver job.

That move created an obvious opportunity, and Martin is officially one of the players taking advantage of it.

Dan Campbell said after training camp that he loved the competitiveness of this year's roster, with Detroit facing difficult decisions across several position groups before Sunday's deadline. Martin becoming part of the 53 is a perfect example of that competition actually changing the roster.

He had also been included on our final Lions 53-man roster prediction.

This time, the prediction survived cutdown day.

articles.title: Chiefs’ Omarr Norman-Lott to begin 2026 season on PUP list
articles.summary: Kansas City is reportedly keeping one second-year defender while another starts the year unavailable.
articles.body:
As we await the Kansas City Chiefs ' final 53-man roster for the 2026 season, or even the initial 53-man roster as of the cutdown deadline at 5:00 p.m. on Sunday, reports have leaked out about who the front office and coaching staff plan to keep.

ESPN's Nate Taylor reported that second-year defensive tackle Marcus Harris will be one of the players going to bed happy on Sunday evening. He will make the team's initial 53-man roster , but Taylor's report is tagged with confirmation of second-year defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott's (Knee) injury status.

Norman-Lott will begin the season on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list, meaning he will miss at least the first four games of the season. The second-round pick from last year's draft is still recovering from tearing his ACL during the Week 7 game against the Las Vegas Raiders last season.

Harris has arguably earned the spot regardless of Norman-Lott's health. He finished the preseason with a standout performance against the Seattle Seahawks , stifling multiple handoffs in the backfield and forcing a lengthy field-goal attempt that was ultimately missed.

Once Norman-Lott is healthy, it will be interesting to see how the rotation adjusts to welcome him back. For now, Harris looks to compete for snaps with rookie Peter Woods behind defensive tackles Chris Jones and Khyiris Tonga.

articles.title: Steelers place DeShon Elliott on IR
articles.summary: Steelers place S DeShon Elliott on IR.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers will be without one of their top defenders in the secondary to start the season. The Steelers have placed safety DeShon Elliott on IR. Elliott will now miss at least the first four games of the season.

After suffering a significant leg injury in Week 8 against the Packers and missing the remainder of the 2025 season, Elliott fought his way back onto the field this training camp. He made his return to live action against the Jets on August 21, but did not play against the Bills on Thursday.

Injuries limited Elliott to only five games last year, totaling 38 tackles, one sack, and one interception. Elliott signed a two-year extension in June of 2025 that keeps him under contract through 2027.

The Steelers' secondary is already thin and missing Elliott is a significant blow. Pittsburgh signed veteran Jaquan Brisker in the offseason and has occasionally deployed Jalen Ramsey at safety, needing to fill a gap left by Elliott. Seventh-round pick Robert Spears-Jennings also made the initial 53-man roster, and veteran Rayshawn Jenkins will also be expected to play a major role in Elliott's absence. The Steelers list Ramsey as a nickel corner, but did play some safety in Mike Tomlin's defense.

The Atlanta Falcons visit Acrisure Stadium for the season opener two weeks from now on September 13.

articles.title: Christian Kirk and Austen Pleasants to begin the season on IR/designated to return
articles.summary: That is not good news for Vederian Lowe
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan hinted at wide receiver Christian Kirk beginning the season on the Injured Reserve with a designation for return. He said the same about Vederian Lowe.

According to Matt Maiocco, that's true for Kirk, but not the case for Lowe. Instead, Austen Pleasants gets that designation. Pleasants is currently dealing with a knee injury. His ability to play tackle and guard may have made him more valuable to the 49ers with the current state of their offensive line.

It also might speak to how serious Lowe's injury was. Lowe suffered a high-ankle sprain at the end of July. I wonder if he had a setback, or if the injury was bad enough that the team didn't think he'd be an option to return early in the season.

It doesn't have to be an either/or. It could mean Lowe is close enough to returning that he doesn't need a designation and can return to practice this week. We shall see.

As for Kirk, it's no surprise that the team will be patient with him. It's one of the benefits of the Injured Reserve. He has experience in ways that Jacob Cowing and Jordan Watkins do not in the NFL as receivers. Plus, Kirk has production. He will add an element to the passing game the Niners have been missing once he returns.

We'll see how both of these moves impact the 49ers once they release their 53-man roster.

The Miami Dolphins had a very busy 48 hours, as they've officially trimmed their roster from 91 players down to 53 over the past two days, becoming compliant with the league rules right at the deadline at 6:00 p.m. ET on Sunday.

While the Dolphins will likely make more moves over the next 48 hours now that there's a new crop of players available, their initial 53-man roster is set.

Hunter didn't play a single game for the Dolphins this preseason, but he makes this list because Miami just acquired him in a trade with the Los Angeles Chargers for wide receiver Tutu Atwell last week. It wouldn't be surprising to see Hunter back on the practice squad if he goes unclaimed on waivers.

Ojabo was one of the free-agent signings that Dolphins fans were most excited about because he was an All-American in his final year at Michigan before tearing his ACL. Unfortunately, he didn't do much in the preseason to earn a spot, but considering Miami needs help in the room, it's a bit surprising that he's no longer on the roster.

Dodson's release is the most surprising move that the Dolphins made, considering he was a starter for Miami in 2025. This just shows how much the team believes in rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez. Even if Rodriguez was going to start, they probably could've kept him around as a backup.

Of all of the free-agent additions at cornerback this offseason, Wilson had the best training camp and preseason, but it wasn't enough to earn a spot in a young, thin room.

The Dolphins brought in Johnson on a one-year deal this offseason, and considering he had seven years of experience in the NFL, it was expected that he'd make the roster. "He's doing well out here playing an edge position. He's instinctive. He's at one of those positions where it's hard to evaluate with what we're doing right now. He can get the alignment, the assignment, all of that. There's a young player that, knock on wood, we feel like is really talented," stated Payton.

articles.title: 'I'm back': Aaron Donald statement calls back to iconic Michael Jordan announcement
articles.summary: In their latest tweet reveling in the un-retirement of Aaron Donald, the LA Rams posted this callback to one of Michael Jordan's most famous moments.
articles.body:
Aaron Donald, one of the greatest defensive players of all-time, is coming out of retirement for one more Super Bowl push with the Los Angeles Rams this season. The 10-time Pro Bowler, eight-time first-team All-Pro and three-time AP Defensive Player of the Year announced his long-awaited decision with a highlight montage on his Instagram account set to "Homecoming" by Kanye West . The final shot shows Donald hugging the Vince Lombardi Trophy after winning Super Bowl LVI in February 2022 with the words "THE RETURN" in bolded caps across the frame.

The Rams ' version of the announcement was much simpler, and perhaps even more fitting.

In a callback to one of Michael Jordan's most iconic moments, the Rams posted a letter addressed to NFL commissioner Roger Goodell and signed by Donald:

On March 18, 1995, Jordan ended his 17-month-long first retirement via press release from his agent, David Falk, with those same two words. The next night, he played for the Chicago Bulls wearing No. 45 in Indianapolis. Jordan eventually switched back to No. 23 and went on to lead the Bulls to a second three-peat before retiring again following his sixth NBA championship in 1998.

Similarly, the Rams are all-in on running it back with Donald with the Super Bowl once again returning to SoFi Stadium, their home stadium where they also won the Big Game four years ago. With a defense that features Donald, Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson, they might just do exactly that .

articles.title: What Buster Posey and Tony Vitello are saying about the Giants manager's future
articles.summary: Buster Posey, the San Francisco Giants' top baseball executive, has made it clear that manager Tony Vitello is in the team's plans for next year. Does Vitell...
articles.body:
Buster Posey , the San Francisco Giants ' top baseball executive, has made it clear that manager Tony Vitello is in the team's plans for next year.

Posey told the Chronicle that he "explicitly" has informed Vitello that he will be back.

"Obviously, he's his own man," Posey said. "I haven't felt once in any conversation that we've had that there's any thoughts about jumping ship. All of our conversations are future-oriented, like, 'What do we have to do to get this right?' So if he wasn't (returning) it would come as a surprise to me."

Vitello talks often and fondly of his college coaching days, understandable since he's less than a year removed from Tennessee, a place he truly loved working. Wistful as he might sound about the Vols and the SEC sometimes, Vitello is a competitor at heart. He's got a challenge in San Francisco and wants to see it through.

"When you get somewhere, you always want to leave it better," he said in a conversation with the Chronicle, "and I'm personally willing to go through hell or high water to do that."

Vitello is under contract for two more years, at $3.5 million per season, with a vesting option for 2029 based on making the postseason in 2028, but his contract has been bought out before - the Giants spent $3 million to free him up from Tennessee.

Vitello is a perennial winner in the college ranks, idolized and with complete power at the Division I level. The Giants, meanwhile, have been beyond disappointing, the major decisions are made above him and the media and fans are far more critical. An awful season is no fun for anyone, but most especially for those in charge.

Vitello is perhaps the greatest recruiter in college baseball history, which always will make him one of the hottest commodities in Division I. Should he show any inkling he'd like to step back into his old world, plenty of deep-pocket schools would be happy to come to some sort of agreement with the Giants to free Vitello up from the remaining two years on his deal.

The only college sport in his immediate future, though, is football, Vitello said.

"The only tie I have to college is I'm super juiced to go to college football games this year, and I still remain loyal to Tennessee," he said. "But now I can go to Tuscaloosa and not be criticized."

Vitello's lack of pro experience has been questioned since Posey hired him last fall and it still pops up as a topic even with the season winding down, especially after this weekend's umpiring crew seemingly raised the issue when Vitello was ejected Friday night. He described the interactions with the crew after he was tossed as getting "personal, real quick."

Because he's the first college coach hired as an MLB manager with no previous pro experience in the modern era, Vitello feels some responsibility to represent that cohort well. When asked about umpires questioning his credentials, for instance, he mentioned that former All-Star Troy Tulowitzki is now a college coach - it works both ways, and he doesn't need to be the poster boy for all things college-to-pro. Milwaukee 's Pat Murphy, the former Arizona State coach, had some pro experience, of course, but he has wowed at both levels.

"People keep throwing in my face, they're cheering for you because they want it to work for other people - and it's already worked for other people," Vitello said.

He just truly believes that some things he and others bring from the top amateur level can translate in the majors, saying that he and director of pitching Frank Anderson, who came with Vitello from Tennessee, "realize a good chunk of what's being done in college can be done here," particularly when it comes to player preparation.

The team's five consecutive non-winning seasons are a first in franchise history. Vitello's primary goal is to get the Giants back to relevance, "and I want to do it right now," he said. "I think we've slowly started to do some things, and I'm willing to go to hell and back to make it look better on the field and for there to be improvement."

Vitello's relationship with veteran players such as Willy Adames , Rafael Devers and Matt Chapman is evolving with the greater familiarity that comes with a full season. "It didn't make sense for me to come in guns blazing," Vitello said, "but now I'm in a different place with those guys."

"Tony is a pretty smart and savvy guy," Posey said. "Most people would agree that if you have a first-year coach, a college coach, come in and be extremely heavy-handed with veteran players, it's probably not going to be the way you want to start. I think he was really aware he needed to prove he was willing to come in and work every day and show he had their back.

"I put my former player hat on and I think if I'm in the clubhouse and a new manager comes in, one that lacks professional experience, and acts like he's got all the answers, it wouldn't go over well."

Posey, who first voiced his desire to bring Vitello back next season to the San Francisco Standard, describes Vitello's fire to win as much like his own.

"I just see him as a guy who, like most all of us, is so competitive that when you get knocked down, you want a chance to figure it out," Posey said. "You want to prove that you can do it."

Teams typically make decisions on the rest of the coaching staff after the season, and with the Giants at the bottom of the NL West most of the way, it's not hard to imagine there might be some changes, but that might not necessarily be the case.

"I'll speak for myself," Posey said, "I think the coaching staff's done a nice job. It's always a hard thing because people are like, 'Well, you're 25-games or whatever under, how can you say they did a nice job?' But I'm watching them every day and the work that they're putting in, some of the improvements that (players) are making; from my vantage point, they've done a nice job.

"Ultimately, my belief is you leave it up to the manager to set it how he wants to set it. Those are conversations that we'll have with Tony for the remainder of the year and into the offseason."

articles.title: Commanders designate two key players to return off injured reserve
articles.summary: The Commanders also placed defensive lineman Deatrich Wise Jr. on the physically unable to perform list
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders placed cornerback Trey Amos and running back Jeremy McNichols on injured reserve with a designation to return on Sunday as part of the team's initial 53-man roster cut.

Also, defensive lineman Deatrich Wise Jr. was placed on the physically unable to perform list. He hasn't practiced at all in camp while recovering from a torn quadriceps during the 2025 campaign.

All three of those guys must miss at least the first four weeks/games.

NFL teams are allowed to designate two players to return off IR that don't count as part of the 53-man roster right at roster cuts.

Amos missed the entire offseason program recovering from a fractured fibula that ended his 2025 season. He dealt with soft-tissue soreness early in training camp, before he was finally cleared to return in mid-August. He suffered an ankle sprain in his second practice back and hasn't returned since. Starting the season on IR will allow him to rehab at a proper pace without taking up a roster spot while doing so.

It's a setback for the Commanders defense, considering he was expected to be their No. 1 cornerback. They'll make do with a combination of Amik Robertson, Mike Sainristil and Rasul Douglas, among others.

McNichols suffered a significant quadriceps injury early in camp and hasn't been back since. He's a versatile veteran who's a solid third-down back and quality pass protector, which is why they wanted him in Washington.

Each team can designate a maximum of eight players to return off injured reserve, though the rest of them must be on the initial 53-man roster of sign with Washington after it's formed.

With uncertainty about whether left tackle Laremy Tunsil (torn triceps) and defensive lineman Johnny Newton (torn pec) can return this season, those guys remain on the active roster for a short while. They'll be moved to IR soon, without the formal designation to return. If it's determined later — both guys had surgery in recent week — that they can't return, the Commanders won't have to burn a return designation.

Tunsil got hurt during a one-on-one rep with edge rusher Odafe Oweh on Aug. 8. It didn't look bad at first, but the severity of the injury came to light later that day. He has since had surgery and is on the path to recovery.

That sent the Commanders offensive line into a spiral, with Brandon Coleman moving to left tackle after previously battling Chris Paul to be the left guard. The front hasn't been the same since. Tunsil will only be of use if the Commanders can be competitive without him and position themselves for a playoff berth.

Newton suffered a torn pectoral muscle during a preseason game against the Miami Dolphins and had surgery on Aug. 19 .
